purpose: Determine whether the finite-prime running-height identity has an established name, separate its routine telescoping core from its useful arithmetic packaging, and bind the exact significance boundary to the reviewer card.

target.statement: If H_0=1 and H_j=b_j H_(j-1), then sum_(j<=N) (b_j-1)/H_j=1-1/H_N; ordering the prime-power jumps of a nonempty finite prime set gives the corresponding unit-mass prime-labelled series.

nearest_prior_work: NIST DLMF Section 2.10(ii), equation 2.10.9, records the standard summation-by-parts finite-difference framework in which sums of consecutive differences telescope to endpoint terms.

Gill and Johansen (1990), printed pages 1501-1502, treat survival functions as product-integrals of hazard measures and explicitly include discrete integrating measures. With S_j=1/H_j and h_j=1-1/b_j, the local mass S_(j-1)h_j=S_(j-1)-S_j is the scalar one-jump specialization.
The exact prime-power event ordering and the 17/2 Fourier boundary-correction consumer are not stated in those sources; they are the local arithmetic packaging.
classification.attribution: Call the abstract result the reciprocal finite-difference telescope, or equivalently a discrete survival/jump-mass identity. Do not present it as a named new theorem or attribute the finite-prime arithmetic statement to survival-analysis authors.
classification.mathematical_interest: The proof depth is minimal, but the invariant formulation is useful: every positive multiplicative height chain carries a canonically normalized reciprocal jump measure, and finite prime sets split that unit mass into labelled prime-power channels with an exact finite residual.
classification.reusable_scope: The endpoint identity applies to every positive multiplicative chain. The separately labelled form applies whenever jump events have unique labels, including finite-prime running LCMs; simultaneous jumps must be grouped before assigning channel weights.
classification.why_it_matters: The honest public story is not a novelty theorem. Its value is exact bookkeeping: in Erdos 269 it proves that the three coordinate-axis masses total one, so the symmetric half-weight contributes exactly 1/2 and the full Fourier correction is exactly 17/2. The finite truncation also exposes the cutoff error as precisely 1/H_P(R).

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: Set S_j=1/H_j. Then (b_j-1)/H_j=S_(j-1)-S_j, so summing is literal endpoint cancellation. Equivalently, with discrete hazard h_j=1-1/b_j, the jump mass is S_(j-1)h_j.
mechanism_comparison.local_arithmetic_step: Order all distinct events p^m<=R. At event p^m the running height multiplies by p, so its jump mass is (p-1)/H_P(p^m) and the label p partitions the total unit mass.
mechanism_comparison.strict_delta: The exact prime-labelled finite truncation, its inclusive-height convention, its consumption by the three-axis Fourier midpoint correction, and the counting-function-weighted value identity are one local summation-by-parts synthesis. None raises the one-line telescope itself above routine status.
mechanism_comparison.scope_sharpening: Primality is unnecessary for the abstract chain. It is used only to make positive prime-power events distinct and hence separately labelable; simultaneous events require grouping. In the weighted refinement, the prime-channel coefficient A(p^m) remains a multidimensional smooth-lattice count, so the channel split is not a one-slope reduction.
